 Jharkhand Raises DA To 63% For Government Employees
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 19, 2026
 # Jharkhand Government
 # Dearness Allowance
 # DA Hike 2026
 # Dearness Relief
 # Government Employees
 # Pensioners
 # Hemant Soren
 # 7th Pay Commission
 # Salary Revision
 The three-percentage-point increase, effective July 1, will benefit around three lakh employees, pensioners and family pensioners across the state
 The Jharkhand government has approved a three-percentage-point increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state government employees, raising it from 60 per cent to 63 per cent. The corresponding Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners and family pensioners has also been increased to 63 per cent.
 The decision was taken at a state Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday. The revised rates will be effective retrospectively from July 1, 2026, officials said.
 The increase will benefit approximately three lakh state government employees and pensioners. Employees drawing salaries under the Seventh Pay Commission will receive DA at the revised rate, while those covered under the Fifth and Sixth Pay Commissions will also receive corresponding revisions.
 Additional Chief Secretary of the Cabinet Secretariat and Vigilance Department Vandana Dadel confirmed the effective date during a press briefing following the Cabinet meeting.
 The revision is intended to provide financial relief to government employees and pensioners against rising living costs. Since the increase is effective from July 1, eligible beneficiaries will also be entitled to arrears for the intervening period, subject to the government's payment arrangements.
 The Cabinet approved a total of 41 proposals during the meeting, covering administrative, infrastructure and social sector initiatives.
 Among other decisions, the government sanctioned ₹37.36 crore for constructing a degree college at Vishrampur in Palamu district and ₹9.75 crore for an observation home in Sahibganj under the Mission Vatsalya scheme.
 It also cleared road development projects worth ₹207.8 crore across Pakur, Saraikela-Kharsawan, Jamtara and Ranchi districts.
 The DA revision follows similar adjustments by other state governments and the Centre, reflecting periodic changes in inflation-linked allowances for public sector employees and pensioners.
